title: Let All the Peoples Praise You
superscription: For the choirmaster. With stringed instruments. A Psalm. A song.

verses.text: May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us, Selah
that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations.
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy, for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth. Selah
Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You.
The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him.

context.author: Not named; the title says only “a Psalm, a song.”
context.genre: Psalm: a song or prayer in Hebrew poetry
context.audience: Israel at worship in Jerusalem, and every reader who prays
context.setting: “May God be gracious to us and bless us, and cause His face to shine upon us” (v.1), the words of the priestly blessing. But the blessing has a purpose: “that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations” (v.2). The refrain calls the world to worship: “Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You” (vv.3, 5). God judges the peoples justly and leads the nations (v.4). “The earth has yielded its harvest; God, our God, blesses us. God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him” (vv.6-7).
context.custom: Priests blessed the people with the words of Numbers 6:24-26 at the end of worship. Harvest was the visible sign of God’s blessing on the land. Jewish tradition reads this psalm during the Counting of the Omer, the 49 days between Passover and Pentecost, which run through the grain harvest.
context.timelineImmediate: Psalm 68 celebrates God marching from Sinai to Zion.
context.timelineBible: God’s promise to Abraham was that “all the families of the earth will be blessed through you” (Genesis 12:3). Simeon called the child Jesus “a light for revelation to the Gentiles” (Luke 2:32). Revelation sees “a multitude too large to count, from every nation and tribe and people and tongue” (Revelation 7:9).

translation.meaning: Produce, harvest, yield of the land.

gospelParallels.note: A light for revelation to the Gentiles.
A great multitude from every nation.

otBackground.note: The LORD bless you and keep you.
All the families of the earth will be blessed.

overview.summary: Israel prays the priestly blessing, asking God to bless them so that all nations will know His salvation, praise Him and fear Him.
overview.settingLine: Harvest fields and the nations watching.

customs.t: Priests raised their hands over the people.

archaeology.t: Silver scrolls with the priestly blessing, about 600 BC.
Silos at Megiddo and elsewhere held the harvest.

overview.discussion: God blesses Israel “that Your ways may be known on earth” (v.2). How might God’s blessings to me be meant for others?
overview.book: The book of Psalms · 150 psalms (1-125 in the app so far). Israel’s songs and prayers: praise, lament, thanks, trust and wisdom, many of them by David.
overview.author: Not named
